rationale: Retain one Gigapower record, add AT&T as the missing 50% co-owner and correct the BlackRock-origin ownership period to the disclosed BGIF IV Neon Acquisition LP vehicle and 50% stake. Regulatory evidence identifies Gigapower, LLC and its predecessor, shows the two partners' aggregate 50/50 ownership and provides the holding vehicles. The joint venture closed and launched in May 2023. Current filings and company releases show continued AT&T ownership and operations. BlackRock's acquisition of the GIP manager did not establish a second GIP economic ownership period, so GIP remains manager context only.

afterImage.name: Gigapower
afterImage.description: Gigapower, LLC is a U.S. wholesale open-access fiber platform formed as a 50/50 joint venture between AT&T and a BlackRock-origin infrastructure vehicle. The company builds, owns and operates multi-gigabit fiber networks that multiple internet service providers can use to serve homes and businesses outside AT&T's traditional wireline footprint. Regulatory filings identify AT&T-related Infrastructure Endeavors Holdings, LLC and Teleport Communications America, LLC as holding an aggregate 50% interest and BGIF IV Neon Acquisition LP as holding the other 50%. The predecessor entity formed in Delaware in February 2022, changed its name to Gigapower in March 2022, and the joint venture closed and launched in May 2023. Current disclosures describe availability or expansion in Florida, New Mexico, northeastern Pennsylvania, North Carolina, South Carolina and southeastern Minnesota, with a long-term target of roughly 1.5 million customer locations. GIP, part of BlackRock, is now referenced as the fund manager, but no separate asset-level transfer or second GIP ownership period was disclosed.
